questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for Complex Differentiability.
questions.answer:
The complex derivative is
\[f'(z_0)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(z_0+h)-f(z_0)}{h}\]

questions.prompt: Use the definition idea to identify the derivative of \(f(z)=z^2\).
questions.answer: Compute the quotient: \[\frac{(z+h)^2-z^2}{h}=\frac{2zh+h^2}{h}=2z+h\] As \(h\to0\), this tends to \(2z\), independent of direction. Thus \(f'(z)=2z\).

questions.prompt: Why is \(f(z)=\overline z\) not complex differentiable?
questions.answer: At \(0\), the quotient is \(\overline h/h\). Along the real axis this equals \(1\). Along the imaginary axis, with \(h=it\), it equals \(-1\). The limit depends on direction, so the derivative does not exist.
